_purpose: Identification terms and target SOC codes for the game-studio triage mode (recipes/case-game-eng-opt-studio-triage.md). Kept as data, not code, so a human can audit and edit the matcher without touching the script.
_provenance: Hand-authored 2026-10-17 by Weiting Wang. The term lists are a HUMAN JUDGMENT about naming conventions in the US game industry, not a record from any dataset. The SOC/O*NET codes are copied from data/bls/compact/soc_occupation_compact.csv (OEWS year 2024); verify a code against that file before adding it.
_warning: A term match is a CANDIDATE, never a verified fact that the company makes games. The Form D industry taxonomy in data/80-days-to-stay/ has no games category (verified 2026-10-17: the 30,369 rows carry only 24 distinct industry labels, none game-related), which is why name/title matching is needed at all — and why its output must clear a human confirmation gate.

studio_terms._strong_note: Matched with a word boundary on BOTH sides. 'engine' is deliberately NOT in this list: as a substring it matches 'Software Engineer' and 'Data Engineer' and produced 905 false positives on this dataset (see the worked run). Word-boundary 'engine' is in ambiguous below.
studio_terms._ambiguous_note: These appear in game work AND in enterprise/medical/adtech work. A company matched only on ambiguous terms is reported in a separate bucket and never promoted to a candidate without human confirmation.

_role_family_note: Matched against top_job_titles_sponsored only. This distinguishes 'this company has sponsored SOMEONE' from 'this company has sponsored someone in MY role family' — the distinction a company-level sponsorship count erases.

target_socs.label: Software Developers
target_socs.why: The code most gameplay/engine/tools programmer titles are filed under on an LCA.

target_socs.label: Video Game Designers
target_socs.why: The only O*NET detail code named for game work; carries game-specific ability/skill levels.

target_socs.label: Special Effects Artists and Animators
target_socs.why: Where technical-artist and VFX work lands when it is filed as an art occupation rather than a computer occupation.

target_socs.label: Computer Programmers
target_socs.why: Included as a downside comparator: the lower-autonomy coding code, useful for seeing the cognitive-pivot spread across the role family.

funding_recency_months._note: DEFINED by the student, not by the SEC: a Form D filing is a point-in-time event with no expiry field. 18 months ≈ a typical seed/Series-A runway before the next raise; past 36 months with no new filing, the last round tells you about the company's past, not its hiring capacity. These two numbers are the mode's most arguable parameter — change them and the Apply list changes.

sponsorship_tiers._note: Thresholds follow the book's Proven/Likely/Unknown language. A blank approvals field is 'Unknown', NEVER 'None': only 1,557 of 30,369 rows in the mapped CSV carry any H-1B approvals value (verified 2026-10-17), so a blank means the join found nothing, not that the company does not sponsor.
